newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW- Venture aims to outpace industry growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW- Venture aims to outpace industry growth.

text.p: Singapore electronics firm Venture Manufacturing aims to outpace growth in the global contract manufacturing industry, company president Wong Ngit Liong said on Thursday.
"In the long run, we want to grow slightly faster than industry growth. Long term means 10 years down the road," Wong told Reuters in an interview.
He added this goal was for both revenue and profits.
According to industry estimates, contract manufacturing in electronics, currently worth about US$60 billion, is seen rising 15-20 percent over the next 10 years, and could even accelerate.

Wong said Venture's performance might fluctuate from year to year and growth in 1997 might not be as tremendous as in 1996, taking into account the slowdown in certain electronics sectors in the first half of the year. He declined to be more specific.
In 1996, Venture posted an impressive 68 percent jump in net profits to Singapore $36.2 million (US$25.3 million) with revenues surging 160 percent to S$649.1 million.
The bulk of Venture's earnings were from contract manufacturing of electronics products like computer periherals, printers, networking systems, data communications and mass data storage products.
Venture was looking to expand its income streams within the electronics sector, Wong said.
"In 1997, we will have more joint ventures and alliances coming up because we are expanding our business globally.
"We are now a bigger company and we have more resources to invest," he said.
Part of Venture's cash hoard of S$126 million would go towards such partnerships and possibly some acquisitions, Wong said.
In April, Venture announced a joint venture with Japan's Sumitomo Electric Industries Ltd to design and make systems electronics products.
The two companies anticipated the joint venture would achieve revenues of s$200 million in the year 2000.
Besides its manufacturing facilities in Singapore, Malaysia and China, Venture had "business centres" in the U.S., Europe and Japan ready to tap opportunities.
"In the next one to two years we would focus on Japan, U.S. and Europe" for new customers, Wong said.

The business centres provide a whole range of services from developing prototype products to customisation, shipping and warehousing. They would also be places for Venture to tap research and development capabilities.
Wong said equally important to its expansion was the development of a pool of talent to manage resources, customers and supplier relationships on a global basis.
On other markets, Wong said Venture was keen on China but would not rush in.
"We just want to plant some seeds there and let demand forces dictate how fast we grow," he said.

Besides a profitable unit in Shanghai, China, which provides contract manufacturing for electronics products, Venture has a 60-percent owned subsidiary Meto First Labelling Systems (Shanghai) Co Ltd there which made a small loss in 1996.
Meto trades in and makes labelling systems.

"Meto is a niche product, very specialised...the department stores and industrial usage (in China) are growing. Once the market there grows, we have a captive base and it just grows bigger and bigger. The longer we are there, the better," Wong
said.
-- Singapore newsroom (65-8703080)
